beats.title: The Roster
beats.body: Professor Permancer passes the bookmark around. Each ribbon answers one name. Penny checks that she can match them without looking at the total. “Again,” he says. The ribbon has already started.
beats.report: Permancer's class practiced matching each returning ribbon to a named traveller, not merely counting them.

beats.title: Ink Has No Conscience
beats.body: Professor Villanelle puts Wicker's sentence on the board. Nobody laughs at it. “Read the verb,” she says. “Now tell me who had to live with it.”
beats.report: Villanelle's class studied the sentence Wicker wrote in the source and asked who bore its consequence.

beats.title: A Letter from Permancer
beats.body:
Reader—

I went back to the Vault before breakfast.

I put the list where Penny held it. I stood where I had stood. Every ribbon pointed home.

Then I walked around it.

The list told me everyone had come home. It had not counted who else crossed. I should have checked both sides before I invited anyone through.

The new procedure is on my desk. There is a blank line at the bottom for what I have still failed to ask.

If you bring back a look from the other side of something, I would like to read it. Penny is making room beside the chalk outline.

—Permancer
beats.report: Permancer wrote to the Reader about the return list's blind side and the procedure he was changing.

beats.title: The Chair's Direction
beats.body: Professor Wispwood turns a chair towards the class. Then towards the wall. “Same chair,” she says. “Which way would you sit?” The chair turns itself back. “Thank you,” she tells it.
beats.report: Wispwood's class tested how the direction of an ordinary chair could change an invitation.

beats.title: Rest After the Door
beats.body: Professor Stonebrook takes the chalk out of the clock's hands. For a little while, the room stops writing the next thing. There's a chair by the window. He sits in the other one.
beats.report: Stonebrook made room for rest after the return rather than assigning another crossing.

beats.title: A Letter from Wicker
beats.body:
I repaired Serenity's map case.

The clasp was always crooked. I used to tell her so. She used to tell me to carry my own map.

I straightened it. Then I tried closing it with one hand and had to put it back the way it was.

She's using it. She hasn't spoken to me about it.

I keep writing another sentence here. I've crossed it out so often the paper's gone soft.

Leave that bit alone.

—Wicker
beats.report: Wicker wrote that he repaired Serenity's map case and left the crooked clasp as she used it.

beats.title: Amendment in the Vault
beats.body: Permancer's notice has a new line: *An invitation can be held open, lit, arranged, or left waiting.* Below it, Penny has written: *Check what it means from the other side.* The notice hangs a little away from the wall so you can read the back.
beats.report: The Vault posted an amended invitation rule and Penny's instruction to check it from the other side.

beats.title: Receipt or Rumor
beats.body: People say the red chair still appears after the East Stacks close. It's facing the right way now. Nobody agrees which way that is.
beats.report: People disagreed about which way the red chair faced after the East Stacks closed.

storyScenes.title: The chair that gets there first
storyScenes.opening:
I've found the Kitchens.

There was a smell coming through my back cover. I followed it. You can follow me.

Ambrose Trencher stands behind a pot big enough to bathe a professor. He's fishing something out with a ladle.

“Bay leaf,” he says.

The thing has legs.

“Ambrose.”

“Then it can leave under its own steam.”

He sets it on the windowsill. It goes.

Serenity Brown has taken a place halfway down the table. Her map is spread between the salt and a heel of bread. There are mountains on it, a river, and a small pencilled sea where she's spilled her water.

She adds a boat.

“Weather,” she says, and moves her bowl uphill.

Wicker Eddies pulls out the chair opposite her.

“That seat's taken.”

“By whom?”

“Someone I haven't met yet.”

“Excellent. They'll be late.”

He sits. Serenity draws a bog on his side of the map.

Wicker steals the pencil. He draws stepping stones across it, each one just too far from the next.

Serenity studies them. Then she draws a very small Wicker in the water.

He leans closer.

“My hair's better than that.”

“It's wet.”

Ambrose puts a bowl between them. Both reach for the bread. Neither lets go.

storyScenes.title: A sentence with its coat off
storyScenes.opening:
Professor Villanelle has written a sentence on the board.

*The ineffable splendour of dawn bestowed a profound sense of possibility upon the weary traveller.*

Something behind the plaster coughs.

Villanelle waits until we've all read it.

“What happened?”

Penny Blackletter raises her hand.

“Someone got up.”

“Where?”

“The sentence hasn't said.”

“What did they see?”

Penny looks at the board again. “It hasn't said that either.”

Villanelle rubs out *ineffable*. The chalk squeals. She keeps rubbing.

“I was at the bus stop,” she says. “I had a headache. Someone had left an orange on the bench.”

She wipes the rest away.

*There was an orange on the wet bench, bright enough that I nearly missed the bus.*

The thing in the wall stops coughing.

I like the orange. I can get my teeth round it.

Serenity has been working on a sentence of her own. Wicker bends sideways to read it.

She puts her hand over the page.

“Ask.”

“Is it about me?”

“It was about something that needed throwing out. I can see why you're hopeful.”

Villanelle reaches between them and takes Wicker's unused paper.

“Your turn.”

He looks at the blank. For once, it gets the first word.
storyScenes.braidText: Villanelle rubbed the grand words off the board. Underneath was an orange on a wet bus-stop bench. I could get my teeth round that.

storyScenes.title: The wrong way to the classroom
storyScenes.opening:
Serenity has lost the classroom.

She knows where it was. She drew a good map yesterday. The corridor has taken this personally.

“We could ask,” I say.

“We're almost there.”

We've passed the same boot three times. It's growing confident.

On the next windowsill sits a paper bird. One wing points left. Written under it are the words *if you want the room*. On the other wing: *if you want the long way*.

Serenity turns it over. There's a tiny drawing of her boat underneath.

“Soren.”

She sounds pleased. Then she frowns at the two wings.

“He could've waited for us.”

Soren Ng is sitting on the stair beyond the left-hand door. He has two chalk stubs and an expression that was clearly meant to look accidental.

“The long way has a glass roof,” he says.

“You put my boat on a bird.”

“It needed to get upstairs.”

She sits beside him to examine the fold. He shows her where the paper turns. Their hands meet at the wing; he lets her finish it.

Wicker comes through the classroom door behind them.

“How elaborate. Have you tried saying hello?”

“Hello, Wicker,” Soren says.

Serenity laughs into the bird.

storyScenes.title: Sunday Book Jump Club
storyScenes.opening:
Professor Permancer lays a ribbon across the floor.

“That end stays here.”

The ribbon immediately crawls towards his shoe.

“Approximately here.”

He kneels, makes a loop, and passes the end through it. He does it again slowly. Penny copies him. Wicker produces a knot that has trapped his thumb.

Permancer frees it without comment.

For this first visit, I’m keeping hold of the ribbon. You don’t owe me a sentence to find the way home.

Permancer touches the ribbon. A little door opens above the knot. Through it I can see his office, including a cup he has been searching for since breakfast.

He puts his hand through, retrieves it, and comes back.

“Now,” he says. “Where was my way home?”

Everyone points at the ribbon.

“Good. Keep looking at it when there's something more interesting to look at.”

nodes.title: Sunday Book Jump Club
nodes.body:
The Vault has polished its handles for Sunday. Even the dangerous ones are keeping still.

Penny checks the list beside the open copy of *Dracula*.

“Permancer. Wicker. You. Me.”

“Still no Dracula?” Wicker asks.

“He lives there.”

“Then he can make the tea.”

“We don't accept food,” Permancer says. “Or shelter. We follow the entrance hall to the first landing. Then we return.”

Ribbons run from his bookmark to each name on Penny's list. I have yours. Don't pull; I'm holding something at the other end.

nodes.title: One verb
nodes.body:
Permancer steps through. Penny follows. The ribbon draws you into the crease.

Words race beneath your shoes. Then stone catches your feet.

The table is longer than it looked. An orange sits at the far end under an unlit chandelier.

I put a corner out to see it better. Penny catches me.

“Observe,” she whispers.

I was observing with my mouth.

A door opens. Dracula comes in.

“You have come a long way.”

He stops beside the table. One hand rests on the chair. A paragraph holds him there.

Wicker moves sideways. Dracula's eyes don't follow.

“He can't see us properly.”

“He's held at this passage,” Permancer says. “It lets the lesson enter without changing his next action.”

“You've pinned him.”

“Wicker. Put the pen away.”

But the pen is already down in the gutter. Wicker writes:

For one sentence, let him choose the verb.

The table draws in its legs. The orange rolls.

Dracula looks at Wicker. Then at you. Then at the light behind you.

“What follows?” he asks.

nodes.title: Every named traveller
nodes.body:
The chandelier burns black.

“Penny, through. You next.”

I pull the ribbon towards the Vault. A word catches in my stitching. I leave it there. I need both covers for this.

Penny reaches the light. You follow.

Wicker backs towards the doorway.

“I gave you one verb.”

Dracula smiles.

“Follow.”

Wicker crosses. Permancer holds the way open behind him.

“Back through. All of you.”

The words reach farther than the ribbon.

Then the professor is home. The source slams shut.

Penny runs her finger down the list. Every ribbon answers. Every named traveller is back.

“Complete.”

Wicker sits on the floor. There's ink on his knee.

At supper he asks where Serenity is.

“Finishing her map,” Ambrose says. “The East Stacks.”

Wicker takes the bowl Ambrose gives him. It goes cold in his hands.

I go back through my stitching for the word I caught on the way home.

The word has gone.

nodes.title: This side of the cover
nodes.body:
You stayed in the Vault. I kept your place here.

Later, Penny brings the Club’s report.

On Sunday, Permancer took the Book Jump Club into Dracula. Wicker wrote a sentence giving the Count a choice of verb. The professor brought every named traveller home; Penny checked the list. Afterwards, a word caught in the Book’s stitching went missing.

storyScenes.title: The East Stacks Incident
storyScenes.opening:
A book lands in Ambrose's soup.

He fishes it out by the spine. *Doors That Should Stay Metaphors.* It drips on his shoes.

Another book falls in the hall. Then another, farther away.

I don't like how they're falling. Books go over like that when somebody's been past them in a hurry.

Ambrose puts down the ladle.

The East Stacks have squeezed their aisles shut. Penny goes sideways between them, following a trail of catalogue cards.

Each says the same thing.

HE WAS HERE.

“Serenity?” she calls.

Ambrose reaches the gap first. He kneels between Travel and Unreliable Geography.

Serenity is against the bottom shelf. Her map lies open beside her. Two small wounds show at her neck.

I shut. I didn't decide to.

“She's breathing. Bring a clean cloth.”

Wicker turns so sharply he hits the shelf. He comes back with three cloths and an empty water jug. He looks at the jug. Goes again.

Permancer's bookmark pulls towards Serenity, then the wall.

“A living anchor.”

Penny catches his sleeve. “Explain.”

“A person from a story has used her to hold himself here.”

“I gave him—” Wicker begins.

“Water first,” Ambrose says.

Serenity opens her eyes.

“Will someone stop turning that page?”

The books are all closed.

She reaches across the floor.

nodes.body:
“His fingers were coming apart,” she says. “I told him he shouldn't be here.”

She looks at the cloth in Ambrose's hand.

“He said he'd found a way to stay.”

Wicker sets the water down. A little spills. He wipes it with his sleeve before anyone can ask.

Serenity sees him.

“What did you write?”

He tells her. The exact sentence. I keep it too.

She shuts her eyes again.

Wicker reaches towards her hand, then puts his own flat on the floor.

“Get my map,” she says to Ambrose.

The Kitchens door appears at the end of the aisle. It has come a long way and left its hinges behind.

Ambrose lifts her. She keeps the map.

A black line travels across its sea, through a mountain, and into the north margin.

Serenity turns her head.

“He's there.”

Permancer takes a step towards the wall.

“Tomorrow,” she says.

He stops.

“Yes. Tomorrow.”

Wicker holds the Kitchens door. Serenity goes through without looking at him.

He stays with the handle long after Ambrose has put her down.

You're still here. I checked twice.

I don't like this aisle now. I'm going to remember where it is, so we never come back to it by accident.

storyScenes.opening:
Before we go anywhere, show me one thing that's here.

The chipped rim of your cup. The sound the fridge makes before it stops. A mark on your hand you've never quite explained.

Pick something near you. Give me a sentence I could find it by.

I'll hold that end.

storyScenes.title: The map with room left
storyScenes.opening:
Soren brings a sheet of tracing paper to the Kitchens.

Serenity is making a tower out of toast crusts. It leans. She's named it after Permancer.

“I've copied the coast,” Soren says.

Her face closes a little.

“For the investigation?”

“For the boat.”

He puts the paper down. He's drawn her little boat in six impossible harbours. One is in a tree.

Serenity looks at them for a long time.

“It'll need a ladder.”

“I wasn't sure how tall.”

She takes his pencil.

I start to close. She puts one finger between my leaves.

“Stay. We need a cliff.”

So I stand on my fore-edge while she draws a ladder up me. It tickles.

At the doorway, Wicker arrives with a repaired map case under his arm.

He sees Soren's paper. He turns the case so the repair faces his coat.

Ambrose takes it from him.

“Tea?”

“No.”

“Then stop standing in the draught.”

Wicker takes a seat at the far end. For the whole of one cup of tea, he has nothing to say about Soren's harbours.

storyScenes.braidText: Soren brought Serenity a map for her boat. Wicker arrived with a repaired map case and stayed for tea. I stood on my fore-edge while she drew a ladder.

storyScenes.title: The Man Reading Himself
storyScenes.opening:
“That one,” Serenity says.

The old reading-room door stands open. Inside, Dracula sits under a green lamp, reading *Dracula*.

He has a pencil. I dislike this before he's done anything with it.

Beside a paragraph he's written:

> He wouldn't have said this.

Penny leans round the door.

“You wrote that?”

“I was present.”

“You can still be wrong.”

Serenity steps into the light. Dracula rises.

“Miss Brown.”

“Serenity.”

He says it correctly. She waits.

Dracula puts his pencil down.

“I've read the last page.”

His hand rests on the closed half of the book.

“Every morning returns me to a sentence I have already lived. You leave a room and something can happen to you. I leave mine because the next paragraph says I must.”

“So you hurt me,” Serenity says.

“I was disappearing.”

“You knew I was a person.”

He looks at her bandage.

“Yes.”

nodes.title: The Man Reading Himself
nodes.body:
“That one,” Serenity says.

The old reading-room door stands open. Inside, Dracula sits under a green lamp, reading *Dracula*.

He has a pencil. I dislike this before he's done anything with it.

Beside a paragraph he's written:

> He wouldn't have said this.

Penny leans round the door.

“You wrote that?”

“I was present.”

“You can still be wrong.”

Serenity steps into the light. Dracula rises.

“Miss Brown.”

“Serenity.”

He says it correctly. She waits.

Dracula puts his pencil down.

“I've read the last page.”

His hand rests on the closed half of the book.

“Every morning returns me to a sentence I have already lived. You leave a room and something can happen to you. I leave mine because the next paragraph says I must.”

“So you hurt me,” Serenity says.

“I was disappearing.”

“You knew I was a person.”

He looks at her bandage.

“Yes.”

nodes.title: The Man Reading Himself
nodes.body:
Dracula opens his book.

“I want a future tense. Yours has been waiting for you all day.”

“And if it costs someone else?” Penny asks.

“I intend to remain.”

Serenity stands. “Then we'd better learn how to send you back.”

His shadow moves first.

It touches the shelf. One book opens onto the sea. Another lets snow into the room. Roses push through a third and catch on Penny's sleeve.

Dracula steps backwards between them.

For a moment he stands in three different doorways.

Then the books close.

Serenity unfolds her map. The black line has split into branches.

Penny pulls a rose thorn from her cuff.

“How many ways?”

“More than yesterday.”

I keep the fallen thorn. It came out of a book and it can still scratch you.
nodes.braidText: Dracula wanted a future tense. Serenity said they must learn to send him back. His shadow opened several books; the black line on her map branched.

storyScenes.report: Penny recorded the meeting in the reading room. Dracula wanted a future beyond his written ending. Serenity confronted him about the harm he had done. He escaped through several books; the black line on her map split into branches.

I've been watching the chair Ambrose leaves pulled back.

Nobody's sitting in it. It still changes the room.

Keep one sentence about how it invites you.

You can leave the place where it is. I want to carry the sentence.

storyScenes.title: The Wrong Castle
storyScenes.opening:
The East Stacks grow a tower overnight.

The bottom is library. The top has stolen a nursery window. Between them, a stair keeps asking for another floor.

A drawbridge hangs over the Quillquarium. The nibs underneath are furious. They've never agreed so completely.

I've read about a tower like this one. It wasn't supposed to get out.

Penny pins up a notice:

> THE EAST STACKS ARE SEVERAL PLACES. PLEASE USE ONE AT A TIME.

Permancer ties ribbons to the banister. Wicker holds the source volume. Serenity studies her map.

“I'm coming,” she says.

“I was about to ask,” Permancer says.

“You're very slow.”

She folds the map into her repaired case. Wicker watches the clasp close. She catches him looking and goes ahead.

Permancer counts us at the door. He counts twice now.

Inside, the stair turns into a corridor. There are three ways through.

I put my ribbon in the door behind us so we can find it again.

nodes.title: The Wrong Castle
nodes.body:
Dracula waits in the central hall. A fireplace blows snow into his coat. Above him, the borrowed nursery window is trying to find morning.

“This isn't my castle.”

“No,” Serenity says. “These are everybody else's rooms.”

A door opens onto a boat in a storm. Permancer wrestles it shut. Seawater soaks his shoes.

“You damaged my source,” Dracula says.

Permancer keeps both hands on the handle.

“We did.”

Wicker opens the book to his sentence. Under it, a second hand has written FOLLOW.

“I thought—”

Serenity waits.

He looks at the map case. At the bandage above it.

“I wanted to see what would happen.”

“You have.”

He lowers his eyes to the page.

The wall splits. Under the stone is a thin fold of paper.

That's paper. I'd know it in the dark. It's the same stuff I'm made of.

Serenity touches it. Her map pulls towards the gap.

“His way back.”

Permancer brings the bookmark near. Its ribbons reach towards the source, the gap, and Serenity.

Penny puts a card beside each.

SOURCE. INVITATION. LIVING CLAIM.

Dracula watches her write.

Serenity puts her own hand over the third card.

“That one's mine.”

Behind us, the sea knocks again.

nodes.title: Supper with a Finished Man
nodes.body:
Ambrose invites Dracula to supper.

“In here?” Penny asks.

“The soup's in here.”

He pulls back a chair. Dracula stops beside it.

“Your invitation is imprecise.”

“Sit down and we'll improve it.”

Ambrose never argues. He just puts food near you.

Serenity takes the place opposite him. Ambrose fills her bowl, yours, his own. He leaves Dracula's empty.

“You presume I don't eat.”

“What would you like?”

Dracula looks at the soup.

“Nothing.”

Ambrose nods and passes the bread.

“I won't return to a finished life,” Dracula says.

Serenity sets down her spoon.

“You're staying by holding on to mine.”

He looks at her. She waits until he looks away.

Ambrose gets a sheet of paper from the recipe drawer. There's a butter mark in one corner.

I'd have found him a clean one. He didn't want a clean one.

nodes.body:
Wicker has covered the Great Hall floor in spoiled menus.

“Blank on the back,” he says before Penny asks.

All that blank. I had to sit on my own corner.

A quill crawls under the first sheet. He lifts the corner and waits until it comes out again.

Serenity sits nearby. Her map case rests against her ankle.

Wicker draws a room. Its first wall refuses to stand.

“Stay flat, then.”

It springs upright.

Penny writes something down.

“You needn't record that.”

“I may teach it.”

Wicker folds a second wall. He's good at this. Even the paper seems annoyed to find it out.

Serenity leans forward.

“Your window's too high.”

“For whom?”

“Anyone who wants to see out.”

He moves it. Their eyes meet through the little opening.

He looks down first.

“I could take the anchor,” he says.

“No.”

“If it would—”

“Fix the window.”

He folds the sill to the right height.

nodes.title: Return by Terms
nodes.body:
Ambrose brings the supper table to the threshold. It wobbles. He puts a folded menu under its short leg.

I'm under the other one, holding the Count's book open. Nobody's putting anything under me.

Dracula reads his signature beside the butter mark.

Permancer signs the Academy's admission underneath.

“No promise of release,” the Count says.

“None.”

“No visit.”

“None.”

He looks at Serenity. She waits beside the open source.

“Poor terms.”

Ambrose puts a hand on the table to steady it.

“They're the ones you signed.”

He reads them twice. I hold. My corner's gone numb.

Dracula steps towards the threshold.

nodes.title: The claim is hers
nodes.body:
At the edge of the source, Dracula turns to Serenity.

“You would send me back.”

She unfolds her map. The black line runs from him into the little kingdom she drew before any of this happened.

“What you changed in me is mine now.”

She puts a finger beneath the line.

“It doesn't belong to you.”

The ink lifts like a loose thread.

“It doesn't hold you here.”

She pulls it free.

His second shadow goes out. The open book drags at his coat.

I hold. A stitch parts in my spine.

Dracula looks into the source. For once, he doesn't know what to say before the page turns.

It turns anyway.

The stair breaks into words. The ballroom sheds its extra centuries. The drawbridge lifts out of the Quillquarium with a flock of nibs hanging from it.

The borrowed moon sails back between two covers.

Then the Great Hall is a hall again.

I wriggle out from under *Dracula*. My loose stitch catches. Penny frees it with her pencil.

Serenity listens.

Somewhere far away, a closed book turns a page.

She picks up her map case.

“Still there,” she says.

Ambrose pulls out a chair.

This time, it's for her.

storyScenes.title: The First Nightbound Morning
storyScenes.opening:
Morning finds Serenity in the Kitchens.

She's built the toast tower again. It has buttresses now.

Sunlight crosses her hands. She turns over a card. A moon. Another card. Another moon.

“Lazy,” she tells the deck.

Ambrose brings tea.

Permancer arrives with a phrase he's plainly been carrying all the way downstairs.

“Residual threshold sensitivity.”

Serenity looks up.

“Is that what the tea's called?”

He sits down.

“What would you call it?”

She looks at the pantry door. Behind it, too far away for anybody else, a page turns.

“Nightbound.”

Penny takes out a card. She waits until Serenity nods.

I make room for the word too.

Permancer puts a new notice on the table.

> Name every traveller. Close the list. Check both sides of the door.

Below that:

> No living anchors.

Serenity takes the pencil.

> Ask me before you make a map of what I can hear.

Permancer reads it and leaves it where she wrote it.

Wicker appears in the doorway. His hair is wet; he's apparently tried to improve it with water and lost.

“May I?”

Serenity turns a card face down.

“Not today.”

He takes his hand off the frame.

nodes.title: The First Nightbound Morning
nodes.body:
Morning finds Serenity in the Kitchens.

She's built the toast tower again. It has buttresses now.

Sunlight crosses her hands. She turns over a card. A moon. Another card. Another moon.

“Lazy,” she tells the deck.

Ambrose brings tea.

Permancer arrives with a phrase he's plainly been carrying all the way downstairs.

“Residual threshold sensitivity.”

Serenity looks up.

“Is that what the tea's called?”

He sits down.

“What would you call it?”

She looks at the pantry door. Behind it, too far away for anybody else, a page turns.

“Nightbound.”

Penny takes out a card. She waits until Serenity nods.

I make room for the word too.

Permancer puts a new notice on the table.

> Name every traveller. Close the list. Check both sides of the door.

Below that:

> No living anchors.

Serenity takes the pencil.

> Ask me before you make a map of what I can hear.

Permancer reads it and leaves it where she wrote it.

Wicker appears in the doorway. His hair is wet; he's apparently tried to improve it with water and lost.

“May I?”

Serenity turns a card face down.

“Not today.”

He takes his hand off the frame.

“All right.”

She watches until he's gone. Then she moves a piece of toast that was holding up the tower.

The tower falls. She laughs, once, at the mess.

“Terrible engineering.”

Ambrose brings more toast.

I want you to have a morning like this one. Not this one. One of yours.

storyScenes.title: Threshold Protocols
storyScenes.opening:
The Academy opened a door. Someone came the other way.

Permancer has written these beside the Vault:

1. Name the source and why you are entering it.
2. Name every traveller allowed to return.
3. Close the invitation around those names.
4. Check the doorway from both sides.
5. Leave the people in the source their own lives. No experiments on them for the sake of a lesson.
6. No living anchors.
7. Ask before using what a changed person can do.
8. After the return, check what came back different.

Penny has pinned the old list beside the new one. The old one is complete. That is why she kept it.

storyScenes.title: After the last lesson
storyScenes.opening:
Serenity is looking at two things on the table.

Soren's folded bird. Her repaired map case.

She opens the case. Wicker has put the new clasp on crooked. It closes perfectly.

“He knows I fasten it with one hand,” she says.

She closes it again, too hard.

“That doesn't help.”

I keep my ribbon still.

“Soren asked about the glass roof. A whole sentence, this time. With a question mark.”

She runs a thumb along the bird's wing.

“I liked that.”

Outside, a pair of quills are arguing over which one gets to be an arrow.

“And I still want to ask Wicker what he meant to happen. Once I think I can bear listening.”

She looks towards you.

“What would you do first?”

nodes.title: The glass roof
nodes.body:
Rain has made the glass roof a second sky. It is full of little falling lines.

Soren is there with two cups and the paper bird. He has written no message on its clean wing.

“You came,” he says.

“I said I would.” Serenity takes a cup. “That was the hard part of the conversation.”

He laughs, then catches himself looking at her neck.

“Ask,” she says.

“Does it hurt?”

“Not now. Sometimes a closed book sounds as if somebody is knocking from inside.”

Soren puts his cup on the sill. He does not ask for a demonstration.

“I could leave,” he says. “If you wanted quiet.”

“The rain is loud enough to hide us both.”

I press my corner against the glass. He offers her the bird, dry inside his coat. Her map case is at her feet. Its crooked clasp catches the light.

“What do you want to tell him tonight?” she asks, almost as if she has forgotten I am listening.

nodes.title: At the table
nodes.body:
The Kitchens are empty except for a plate Ambrose has left beneath a cloth. Wicker sits at one end of the table. Serenity takes the other. She puts her map case between them, not as a bridge.

“I thought one sentence could make him choose a harmless verb,” Wicker says.

“You wrote a way for him to choose.”

“I did.”

He keeps his hands on the table where she can see them. He is usually quick enough to make a joke before a hard word lands. I wait for one. None comes.

“I was angry when you asked to take the anchor,” she says. “You kept trying to pay for what happened with yourself. That would have made another person carry you home.”

“I know that now.”

“You knew I said no.”

“Yes.”

The cloth lifts at one corner. Ambrose has left two slices of pear tart. Neither reaches for it.

Wicker looks at the crooked clasp he fitted to her case. “I can fix that.”

“It works.” She touches it once. “You can answer the question I came to ask. What will you do differently at the next door?”

He takes a breath. “Ask who has to live on the other side of it.”

She does not forgive him. She does not leave. That is the length of this table tonight.

She looks down at the blank back of her map. What should the next line between them be?

nodes.title: A greenhouse evening
nodes.body:
Serenity takes the path behind the greenhouses. Neither folded bird nor repaired map case is a summons. She has brought both because they are hers.

The little greenhouse is still warm from the day. A moth is asleep on the watering can. She sits beside it and takes out a card.

On one side she draws the pantry door. On the other, the path she took here. She can hear a page turning somewhere no one else can hear it. She lets it turn.

Penny stops outside with two paper cups. “I can leave one,” she says. “Or both.”

Serenity opens the door a little. “You have exactly one minute to tell me whether the Vault notices are still arguing.”

“Seven minutes. Permancer used a colon.”

Serenity laughs and takes a cup. Penny waits. Serenity has an evening of her own, whether or not she shares some of it.

She looks at the second chair, then at the empty path. Which part of the evening should I keep?

bleedArticles.title: Every Listed Jumper Home
bleedArticles.body:
A supervised Jump into *Dracula* ended early after Wicker Eddies wrote an unauthorized sentence in the source margin. The sentence read: *For one sentence, let him choose the verb.*

Professor Permancer opened the return. Every registered entrant answered the bookmark's check. The source is closed while the annotation is examined.

“I meant it,” Eddies said when asked whether it was a prank.

Permancer has asked the Bleed to print the exact sentence. We have.

bleedArticles.title: Serenity Brown Awake
bleedArticles.body:
Serenity Brown is awake in the Kitchens after an attack in the East Stacks. Count Dracula crossed out of his source during Sunday's return and deliberately used the wound to hold himself in Academy space.

Brown can hear page-turns from closed books. She is deciding what help she wants to give. Reports go to Penny Blackletter; visits go through Ambrose. No further injury has been reported.

Permancer has confirmed that he opened the return invitation. Eddies has confirmed his alteration to the source. Both are assisting the investigation.

bleedArticles.title: Several Places, One Entrance
bleedArticles.body:
A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks. The Quillquarium drawbridge is real and closed to visitors. The nursery window belongs to a neighboring book. Please don't take it home.

Dracula's absence from his source is pulling other stories into the gap. The Academy has reconstructed the return conditions: source, invitation, and withdrawal of the living claim.

Serenity Brown has agreed to the controlled return. The final condition is hers to release.

bleedArticles.title: The Count Returned
bleedArticles.body:
Dracula is back in *Dracula*. The borrowed rooms have returned to their books.

Serenity Brown still hears the crossings. She has named the change Nightbound and asked us to print it. She was in the Kitchens this morning, complaining about her cards.

The Vault's new return list names every permitted traveller and must be checked from both sides. Permancer has suspended ordinary teaching Jumps while the safeguards are fitted. The school will publish the reopening when it has one.

Eddies helped close the breach. The original annotation remains in the record.
